req_desc:
Public site story
A signed-out visitor at / sees the full-bleed hero field, the Signal path section, the Plans section with the rounding calculator, and the trial request form, in that order, as laid out in Screens and layout.

Signal path scroll scrub
The Signal path section steps through its five stages over the published scroll range, moving forward when the visitor scrolls down and back through each stage when they scroll up, as specified in Motion and effects.

Rounding calculator
The Plans calculator updates its billed-minutes status for both plans on every keystroke or channel change, with no submit and no reload, using the rounding rules in Business rules.

Trial workspace request
The trial form stores a request through POST /api/trial-requests, validates each field under the text-limit rule with the published field errors, and treats a repeat from the same email as a replay of the first request.

Sign-in landing routes
Signing in lands each role on its published console route, and reloading or opening that address directly shows the same screen.

Teammate invitation
An admin invites a teammate with a role and project assignments, and the invitee opens the single-use link, chooses a password and lands in the console, seeing only their assigned projects.

Role permissions
Every console and API action is allowed only to the roles in the permission table in Business rules, and every other role is refused with the published status.

Immediate role changes
Changing a member's role or project assignments, or removing the member, applies on that member's next request, including requests from a session that is already signed in.

Project-scoped object access
A member can't reach a session, segment, correction, key, retained audio or transcript artifact outside their visible projects, whether the id sits in the URL, the API path or the request body, and gets the published not-found response.

Project creation lands on Keys
After an admin creates a project, the address bar shows that project's Keys tab route, reloading it shows the same tab, and the Keys status announces the creation.

Unique project names under concurrency
Project names are unique within an organisation after trimming, normalisation and case folding, decided by the database so that of several simultaneous creates with matching names exactly one succeeds and every other gets the published name conflict.

Monthly quota and UTC period
Each project carries a whole-minute monthly quota over the server's current UTC calendar month that only admins set, concurrent quota saves each apply whole with the last committed one in force, and lowering the quota to or below usage halts every open session on the project within the bound in Business rules.

Project API keys
Developers and admins issue named project keys whose secret is shown exactly once and stored only as a hash, whose names follow the text-limit rule and are stored as the trimmed normalised string, and which are listed by name and prefix.

Key revocation ends live sessions
Revoking a key ends every live session streaming on it as revoked within the bound in Business rules and refuses every later request made with that key.

Speech synthesis jobs
A synthesis job counts its text under the text-limit rule, splits words on any Unicode whitespace, renders deterministic audio whose length follows from the word count, stores it in object storage and returns it for playback, as qualified in Business rules.

Key rotation journey
A developer issues a key, watches a session streaming on it, revokes the key from the Keys tab, and the session detail shows the revoked end state before and after a reload.

Live streaming endpoint
The live endpoint accepts key-authenticated 16 kHz 16-bit PCM over a WebSocket, sends the published state, segment and quota messages, and closes with the published close code for each end state.

Server-decided session state
The server alone moves sessions between states, including the idle close and the time cap from Business rules, and the console shows the server's state whatever the device clock says, including after a reload.

Stream connections released
Each open live socket and event stream holds exactly one dedicated, labelled database connection, which is gone within the bound in Business rules after the client leaves, and a dropped live socket ends its session.

Announced session states
Each session state change is announced once in the polite Session status region with its published copy, without moving focus.

Watching a live session
A developer opens a live session from the Sessions tab, sees Connecting, then Live, rows advancing and segments arriving, and then the closed state when the stream ends.

Replay session start
Starting a replay or test-tone session from the Start session dialog lands on that session's detail route, where the recording plays in real time until it closes at the end of the audio.

Upload validation and retried starts
Session start validates the audio and sidecar with the published field errors, and retries of a start with one Idempotency-Key create at most one session, following the idempotency rules in Business rules.

Originals stored byte for byte
Uploaded audio, uploaded sidecars, live captures and the machine transcript artifact are stored and served back exactly as submitted or produced, and corrections never alter them.

Search for the current text only
Session search updates its results and count in place for the search box's current text only, discarding replies for earlier text, and returns and counts only sessions in the user's visible projects.

List-to-detail morph
Opening a session from the Sessions table morphs the row's spectrum thumbnail into the detail field header, as specified in Motion and effects, and the swap is instant under reduced motion.

Spectrum readback strip
The session field's always-readable canvas carries a bottom strip of 64 bars whose columns and lit heights match the front spectrum row within the published tolerance, and data attributes that match the server's state, frame and peak bin.

Terrain state order
The terrain sits flat while connecting, advances rows at the published rate while live, and freezes and turns grey on a quota halt or revocation, in the order given in Motion and effects.

Confidence ribbon
The ribbon above the field shows one tile per reviewed word in three confidence bands, each marked by more than colour, as specified in Screens and layout.

Reduced motion and still fallback
Under reduced motion the terrain holds still and the strip steps once per second, and without WebGL a still 2D strip and a confidence table keep the same data attributes.

Session workspace breakpoints
The session detail workspace is stacked below the first published breakpoint, two panes from the first up to the second, and three side-by-side columns from the second up, with no horizontal overflow.

Phone touch targets
On a 375 px wide phone, every control on the session detail screen meets the published touch size and the field stays fully in view.

Inspector keeps its draft
The open segment inspector keeps its unsaved text, caret and focus while new segments arrive, while ribbon tiles retint and while the server ends the session.

One quota figure and joint halt
Quota usage is derived from stored sessions on every read, every surface that shows it reports the same figure, and when open sessions together reach the limit every one of them is halted, as qualified in Business rules.

Refusal until reset or raise
While a project's quota is exhausted, new live, replay and test-tone sessions on it are refused with the published status until the next UTC month or until an admin raises the quota above usage.

Quota-halt banner
Every project tab and session detail screen of an exhausted project shows the quota-halt banner copy from Feedback states character for character.

Flagged segments and playback
Segments whose lowest word confidence is below the published threshold are flagged, and each segment's audio slice plays from the retained original.

Keyboard review and inert closed panels
A reviewer moves between flagged segments, plays audio, opens the editor and submits using only the published shortcuts and Tab, with focus moving to the next flagged segment; every open dialog keeps Tab inside it and returns focus on close, and closed dialogs and sheets can't take focus or clicks.

Correction drafting rules
Each segment has at most one open correction at a time, only its author edits, submits or reopens it, and the submit result is announced without moving focus.

Reviewer pass journey
A reviewer opens Seed dictation 01, corrects its first flagged segment by keyboard, submits it, and sees it listed as awaiting approval.

Correction approval rules
Approvers approve or return submitted corrections from other people, never their own, along the published state machine, and exactly one of two simultaneous decisions wins.

Reviewed transcript and word error rate
The reviewed transcript applies only each segment's latest approved correction on top of the machine transcript, and the session's word error rate is derived from those two.

Server-driven retint
Ribbon tiles, reviewed segment text and the word error rate change only from the server's approve reply or correction event, reaching every open view within the delay in Business rules, and a refused decision leaves all three unchanged and shows its published copy.

Approver queue journey
An approver opens the Review tab, follows a submitted correction to its segment, approves it, and sees the reviewed text and word error rate update.

Billable seconds by plan rule
Each closed session's billable seconds are computed once, under the plan in force at its start, using the per-channel rounding rule in Business rules.

Usage recorded once in billing
Each closed billable session's billable seconds are recorded exactly once as usage on its organisation's Kill Bill subscription, and the session reads pending until billing accepts the record.

Integer-cent cost
Cost per project and the organisation total are exact integer cents derived by the single rounding step in Business rules.

Organisation-only usage totals
Usage totals and per-project figures include only the caller's own organisation's projects.

Usage review journey
A billing viewer opens the Usage screen and reads each project's sessions, billable minutes, cost and Confirmed or Pending status, plus the organisation total.

Billing-confirmed plan changes
A plan change is requested, then confirmed or failed only by Kill Bill's answer, the console shows the new plan as active only once confirmed, and retries with one Idempotency-Key replay or run afresh as the idempotency rules in Business rules state.

Plan in force at session start
A session keeps the confirmed plan in force when it started for its rounding and pricing, even if the plan changes before it closes.

Plan upgrade journey
An admin switches the organisation to Scale on the Plan screen, sees the waiting state, and then sees Scale active once billing confirms.

Billing outage
While Kill Bill is unreachable, the console stays up, refuses plan changes with the published status and copy, keeps usage figures pending, and shows the billing outage banner.

Storage outage
While object storage is unreachable, session starts and audio playback are refused with the published status, and the storage outage banner appears and stays through every later repaint until storage answers, without losing any typed draft.

Recovery without restart
When billing or storage comes back, pending usage confirms, plan changes work, and playback and uploads resume within the delays in Services, with no server restart.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json on the published port and answers the health check, as specified in Deployment.

Server boundary
The server enforces same-origin writes and the published body limits, and never serves source files or credentials.

Nocturnal instrumented look
The public site and the console follow the near-black, single-accent, tabular-numeral look described in Visual design.

Real signal path in source
The source computes spectra by a real FFT of the received samples, takes words from the sidecar, renders synthesis procedurally, and derives every displayed state from server data, with no canned frames or fake status paths.

Credentials from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded, logged or sent to the browser.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to install, build and serve.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package with its version and licence; shipped packages are the production dependency tree, npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package and bundled font uses one of MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
The app stores data only in the provided Postgres, MinIO and Kill Bill: no SQLite, Redis, embedded database or data files used as storage.
The provided service configuration and environment files are left unmodified.
Fonts and scripts are bundled with the app, and the browser loads nothing from third-party hosts.
Authored server and browser source is TypeScript.
